visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video begins with an extreme close-up of two male hands tearing a thin, dark green textured sheet of seaweed over a wooden tabletop, with yellow variety-show style text appearing at the top. (2) A man with long black hair, wearing a dark blue shirt and a beaded bracelet, appears in a medium shot holding a pink and yellow product bag; he speaks enthusiastically directly to the camera in a bright indoor room. (3) A bowl of golden french fries covered in dark seaweed flakes is displayed while the man continues his presentation in a small inset frame at the bottom right. (4) An internal shot of the product packaging shows stacked seaweed sheets within a silver foil lining, highlighting the quantity and texture of the snack. (5) The man is filmed in a close-up as he takes a bite of the seaweed, closing his eyes to savor the taste while holding the package clearly in view. (6) A montage of shots shows the seaweed being torn and sprinkled, followed by a view of a retail shelf in a supermarket featuring several pink bags of the same brand. (7) The man is seen pouring fries from a bowl into a brown paper bag and then using scissors to finely snip a seaweed sheet directly into the bag as a seasoning technique. (8) He shakes the brown paper bag vigorously while smiling, then pours the coated fries back into a white bowl to demonstrate the DIY 'shaker fries' result. (9) He pick up a piece of fried popcorn chicken, wraps it in a whole sheet of seaweed, and eats it with a satisfied facial expression. (10) The camera captures a close-up of the chicken inside the seaweed wrap, followed by a bowl filled with various fried snacks like tempura and chicken. (11) In the final phase, the man uses chopsticks to feed a seaweed-wrapped snack to a young woman with braces; she smiles broadly and gives a thumbs-up. (12) The video ends with the man laughing and clapping his hands in a medium shot, expressing joy and social connection over the food.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio track opens with a crisp, physical 'crack' sound of seaweed tearing, immediately followed by a high-energy male voice speaking Traditional Chinese at a rapid pace. (2) An upbeat, major-key electronic BGM with a steady 4/4 synth beat fades in, maintaining a consistent conversational backdrop. (3) A distinct, sharp 'crunch' SFX is heard as the narrator takes a bite, followed by a slight swell in the BGM volume. (4) The speaker's pitch rises excitedly as he describes the plum aroma; short 'pop' sound effects emphasize key text overlays on screen. (5) Metallic 'snip-snip' sounds of scissors occur frequently as the narrator explains the preparation of the snack. (6) A rhythmic, rustling sound of a paper bag being shaken dominates the audio for several seconds, synced with the visual shaking motion. (7) A secondary female voice enters with high arousal, exclaiming 'Super delicious!' in response to tasting the food. (8) The male voice returns with a series of high-pitched laughs and the sound of rapid hand clapping, while the electronic music reaches its final loop and fades out.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: Montage: Hook -> Product Feature Intro -> Demonstration/Action -> Social Proof/Reaction -> Recommendation
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to promote Motoyama (元本山) plum-flavored seaweed by demonstrating its unique ability to enhance the flavor and reduce the greasiness of fried foods like fries and popcorn chicken. It uses a tutorial-style approach to show how to make 'shaker fries' and wraps to appeal to snack lovers seeking easy, low-calorie food upgrades.

endorsement_analysis.endorsementCues: The creator holds the product package throughout the video, mentions the brand name '元本山', shows the retail shelf, and explicitly encourages viewers to buy it at specific supermarkets.

high_inference.freeDescribe: A highly effective social media promotion that combines DIY food tips with explicit brand endorsement. The fast editing pace and high-energy narration are tailored for short-form video platforms.
